findings.summary: Linked product cards still don't lift on hover, in light or dark. In the hover capture every card sits flush: none moves -4px and none gets the hard offset shadow, so the hovered card looks like all the others. The spec now has the .lift-card recipe, a 'Linked cards' paragraph and a row in the Interaction table, and the build still leaves the card's hover out. This is the third round this is carried over (rc.2, rc.3, rc.4). The hard lift on linked cards is where the reference shows its signature most.
findings.promptFix: Make the card lift part of building the card, not an optional recipe to apply later. Any card that is a link or is clickable, or whose wrapper is, gets .lift-card on its outermost bordered element in the same change that creates the card component. That element also gets 8px of clearance, and no ancestor of it may have overflow: hidden. Add a required step to Verification: in each theme, hover the first card of every card grid and read its computed translate and box-shadow. Translate must be -4px -4px and box-shadow must not be none. If either check fails, the build is not done, whatever else changed.

findings.summary: Two pink actions show at once on the dashboard's empty-filter state, in light and dark: the band's always-visible 'Refresh' and the empty state's 'Clear filters'. This regresses from rc.3, where both were ink. Refresh is now pink by default, and the empty-state component adds its own pink button without checking what pink is already in view. The spec forbids exactly this.
findings.promptFix: A page-header, band or toolbar action that is always on screen (refresh, export, share, settings) is lift--ink or lift--ghost, never pink. Pink belongs to the one action the screen's current state is about: the form submit, the empty-state or error recovery, the dialog confirm, the main CTA. When a component brings its own button, it gets pink only if nothing else pink is in view. In the final check, render every state at the desktop viewport and count the pink-filled buttons: exactly one, plus small tags.

findings.summary: At phone width, tables keep their desktop columns and scroll sideways inside their box with no cue. On the security screen only Device and Location are visible: Last active and every Revoke row action are off-screen, and the location text runs into the box's right border, so the screen's main task can't be seen. The team table has the same problem: it looks like a complete two-column table, and its other columns are found only by swiping. The spec's 'tables scroll inside their bordered box' rule has no exception for row actions and asks for no cue.
findings.promptFix: Under breakpoint.md, a table whose rows carry actions never hides those actions behind sideways scroll. Reflow each row into a stacked block inside the same bordered box: the primary cell as the title, the other cells as label/value lines, and the row action visible at the end. Keep internal sideways scroll only for read-only tables that don't fit, and make the overflow visible: size the columns so the last visible one is cut part-way, with space.12 of padding before the border, and never let cell text touch the border. Verify at 390px that every row action is on screen without scrolling the table and that every scrolling table shows a cut-off column.

findings.summary: In dark mode the empty-state coin sticker's outline and glyph turn paper-white, because the recipe strokes with currentColor set to color.text.primary. The product stickers on the same site keep black ink outlines, and a white plus on pink is weak.

The blog's empty search result puts the yellow band inside a bordered card as its header strip. Bands are page or section headers and never go on cards. The spec's 'empty state (band above the sticker)' wording invites this.
In dark mode, hovering a table row shows no visible fill. The hovered row has the same raised gray as the other rows, while the light theme shows the subtle fill.
On mobile, the horizontally scrolling pill strip clips a focused pill's outline at the top and bottom, so only the two side arcs of the ring show.

On desktop, the settings screens put their content in a narrow column of about 60% of the container, pinned left under a full-width band. That leaves a large empty strip on the right, where the reference fills its container with dense content.
On the desktop project detail page, the status pill sits alone at the band's far right edge, on the meta line and away from the title it describes. Mobile puts it right under the title.

notes: Review: 131/131 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.4/review-1).

Review: 131/131 checklist items by 8 reviewers and the lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.4/review-1). I opened the card-hover, empty-filter and mobile security screenshots to confirm the three majors.
No blockers. The hidden Revoke actions can still be reached by swiping inside the table, so the task is hidden, not broken. The reference's identity holds.

Merged: the dashboard reviewer's minor about the team table having no scroll cue and the settings reviewer's major about the hidden sessions-table actions are one rule (mobile tables that scroll inside their box, with no cue and no reflow). I graded them together as one major, caused by the spec. I marked the blog's band-inside-a-card minor as caused by the spec, because of the spec's 'empty state (band above the sticker)' wording.

Fixed since rc.3: the open account-menu trigger is no longer pink (that major is resolved), the loading button on the band is readable with the coin turn, the about page's stock icon is now ink-outlined stickers, the sweater sticker is a different drawing from the tee, and product pages mark the current 'Shop' pill.
Regression from rc.3: the always-on dashboard Refresh became pink, so the empty state shows two pink actions.

The four apps clearly look like one family: paper and ink, regular-weight display type, one full-width band per section with an ink rule under it, ink current-page pills (paper in dark), outlined cards, pink price tags and the same dark mapping everywhere.
Someone who knows the reference would recognize it from the yellow sticker hero with tilted, cropped coins and the flooded shop band over a dense, colorful wall of different sticker products.

Signature elements: bands, outline pills and sticker art hold across all apps, and the lift shows on buttons. The hard lift on linked cards is still missing after three rounds, which suggests the agent treats the recipe as optional. The fix makes it part of the card component and a verification step the build must pass.
Not passing: three majors (card lift, two pink actions, mobile tables hiding row actions).
